title: Temperature-induced effective topology in many-body ultracold atomic quantum systems
authors: Nitya Cuzzuol, Michele Miotto, Arianna Montorsi, Giacomo Valtolina, Luca Barbiero
abstract: Ultracold atomic quantum systems offer an unprecedentedly powerful platform for exploring interacting symmetry-protected topological phases. Here, we show that their characteristic control over temperature provides a resource for engineering effective topological regimes with no zero-temperature counterpart. Employing finite-temperature matrix-product-state calculations, we investigate experimentally accessible Hamiltonians - the interacting bosonic Su-Schrieffer-Heeger and spin-1 XXZ chains - that host a topological phase at zero temperature, as well as a fermionic dipolar ladder model whose ground state exhibits no topological order. By tracking complementary topological markers, we identify an intriguing mechanism rooted in the structure of the zero-temperature phase diagrams: in finite-size systems, excitation gaps with different magnitudes define an intermediate-temperature window where the correlations associated with the lower gap are suppressed, while those protected by the larger gap persist. This enables the emergence of effective finite-temperature regimes exhibiting topological features that are either absent or qualitatively different from those at zero temperature. Our results establish a novel route toward exploring effective topological phases in ultracold atomic quantum systems.
summary: This paper demonstrates that temperature can act as a tunable resource to engineer effective topological phases in ultracold atomic quantum simulators. By analyzing gap structures in models like the SSH chain, the authors show that intermediate temperatures can stabilize topological correlations that are absent or different from the zero-temperature ground state. This opens a new experimental avenue for realizing and studying topological matter.
main_problem: The study investigates whether temperature itself can serve as a resource to engineer effective topological quantum phases in many-body systems that do not exist at absolute zero temperature.
main_result: The research establishes a novel mechanism where finite-temperature thermal fluctuations can drive systems into effective topological regimes, distinct from their zero-temperature ground states.
method: The analysis employs finite-temperature matrix-product-state (MPS) calculations, comparing results with zero-temperature DMRG calculations to track topological markers.
model_or_system: The work focuses on ultracold atomic quantum systems, modeling interacting bosonic Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) chains, spin-1 XXZ chains, and fermionic dipolar ladder models.
key_observables: Long-range order (LRO) of non-local string correlation functions (SCFs), entanglement spectrum (ES), and the gap structure defined by different excitation gaps.
important_parameters: Temperature (T), interaction strengths (V, $\delta J$), and the specific gap magnitudes ($\Delta E_{Cb}, \Delta E_{Nb}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on finite-size systems and the applicability of MPS methods to the thermal state purification.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically illustrates the optical superlattice potential used for the dimerized model.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the $T=0$ topological phases in specific models, then introducing finite-temperature calculations to observe how thermal fluctuations modify or induce new effective topological behaviors by selectively suppressing certain excitation gaps.
why_interesting: This is highly relevant for AMO physicists as it provides a concrete, experimentally accessible mechanism (temperature control) to tune and explore exotic quantum phases in ultracold atomic setups.
